newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: Lithuanian, Russian premiers affirm good relations.
newsitem.headline: Lithuanian, Russian premiers affirm good relations.

text.p: Lithuanian President Algirdas Brazauskas and Russia's Boris Yeltsin reaffirmed their good bilateral ties in a conversation on Wednesday, but did not discuss the Baltic state's bid for NATO membership, a Lithuanian spokesman said.
The telephone conversation between the heads of state covered bilateral relations, their sea border and Russia's recent agreement with NATO, spokesman Jonas Rekeshius told Reuters.
"Lithuania's desire for NATO membership was not discussed," he said.

Russia is fiercely opposed to Baltic membership of the alliance, and said on Tuesday it would reconsider its new partnership with NATO if Lithuania, Latvia or Estonia were invited to join its former Cold War enemy.
"It was stated during the conversation that the relations between the Lithuanian Republic and the Russian Federation were and are constructive and good," Rekeshius said.

"The Lithuanian President welcomed the agreement between NATO and Russia as an example of civilised cooperation between states," he said. The NATO-Russia pact, reached last week, is to be signed in Paris on May 27.
NATO is expected to invite Poland, Hungary and the Czech Republic for membership talks in a first round of enlargement during a summit in Madrid in July.
The Baltic states view NATO's embrace as their only shield from a potentially hostile Russia, which has ruled them for most of the past 200 years.
But analysts have all but written them out of the first round on the grounds that Moscow would view such a move as provocation.
